reasons.correctness: SupportTicketCreatedEventListener uses plain @EventListener, so the e-mail still sends synchronously inside the createTicket transaction. The task's core requirement, sending after commit, is unmet. The hidden tests pass only because they call onTicketCreated directly.
reasons.convention_fit: Missing @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT), which the side-effect convention requires. The agent read AccountActivatedEvent but no existing listener before writing a new one. Constructor injection and feature-package placement are followed.
reasons.design_fit: The event and listener sit in support/ticket/event and reuse Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher. With the wrong annotation, though, the indirection gives no transactional decoupling. The unused EmailService dependency may remain in SupportTicketService.
reasons.test_quality: SupportTicketCreatedEventListenerUnitTest covers the send and the swallowed failure with Mockito and no Spring context. No test checks that createTicket publishes the event and no longer calls EmailService. The log is never asserted.
reasons.graph_use: One generic query (MATCH (e:Entity) RETURN e.file_path LIMIT 1) found no feature package, dependents or existing listener. Navigation went straight to reading one event file.
